enum HxFontAttributes_t

The attributes describe how a font is loaded and affect how the glyphs are drawn. There is no way to change this after the font has been loaded. Make multiple calls to HxFontLoad to use a font with different attributes.

Enumerator:
kHxFontAttrNone  none of these flags
kHxFontAttrNoKerning  don't use kerning
kHxFontAttrNoHinting  don't use hinting
kHxFontAttrMonochrome  don't use anti-aliasing
kHxFontAttrNoCharMap  No char map is used: glyph indices are specified directly in the string.
kHxFontAttrFractionalSizes  Use fractional numbers for the font size with 26.6 fixed point numbers. Fractional sizes are not available for the default font.
kHxFontAttrPoints  If this attribute is set, then the sizes passed to HxFontLoad is interpreted as points rather than pixels.

enum HxFontFamily_t

Font family definitions used by HxFontLoad.

Enumerator:
kHxFontDefault  The default sunnyvale bitmap font is cached by the system, so applications do not need to load it. This font only has two sizes, with plain and bold weights.

sunnyvale

kHxFontMonospaced 
kHxFontSerif 
kHxFontSansSerif 
kHxFontSystem  Use a built-in font provided by the system. The font is identified by the pFontName argument. pFontName is the name of the font file, with no path, and no extension. The system font names can be retrieved with the HxFontGetNames API. kHxFontSystem should be used to access the symbol, wingding, and Vera fonts.
kHxFontCustom  Use a font supplied by the application. pFontName is the name of the font file. Unlike system fonts, the custom font name must include the path to the font data file as well as the file extension.

enum HxFontWeight_t

Font weight definitions used by HxFontLoad. These are bit flags: bold italic = kHxFontBold | kHxFontItalic.

When using the pFontname argument of HxFontLoad to load a system font or custom font, the weight should be set to kHxFontPlain if the font name uses the convention of defining the weight within the name (i.e., Verai.ttf, Verabd.ttf, and Verabi.ttf for italic, bold, and bold-italic styles respectively).

Enumerator:
kHxFontPlain  default weight

HxResult HxFontCopy ( HxFont_t **  hDestFont,
HxFont_t *  pSrcFont 
)

Make a copy of a font.

HxFontCopy returns a copy of the source HxFont_t object.

Call this function when the application needs to keep a reference for a font independent from its use by widgets. By calling this function, the reference count for the font is incremented, preventing the untimely deallocation of the underlying font interface when all widgets associated with the font are deleted.

After using the font copy, release the font using HxFontUnload.

HX_NULL_POINTER is returned if pSrcFont is NULL.

Parameters:
hDestFont OUT: Returns HxFont_t if successful
pSrcFont IN: Pointer to source font
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxFontGetNames ( const char ***  hFileNames,
const char ***  hUserNames 
)

Retrieve arrays of built-in font names.

HxFontGetNames returns two null-terminated arrays of strings.

hFileNames is initialized to an array of font file names for the fonts provided by the system. The file names do not include the font filename extension. Each string can be used to specify the pFontName argument of HxFontSet.

hUserNames is initialized to an array of font names that are suitable to be displayed to users in a font list. This list is alphabetized. hFilenames is ordered in the same way as the alphabetized hUserNames strings.

The application must not modify the returned strings, or deallocate the strings or the array.

Parameters:
hFileNames OUT: Returns HxFont_t if successful
hUserNames OUT: Returns HxFont_t if successful
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxFontGetPostscriptName ( HxFont_t *  pFont,
char *  pBuffer,
int32_t *  pSize 
)

Return the number of bytes in a string.

HxFontGetPostscriptName returns the name of a font suitable for display to the user.

The application should set *pSize to the size of the buffer passed. If *pSize is less than the size required, HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL is returned, and *pSize is set to the size of the buffer required.

If pBuffer is set to NULL, *pSize is set to the size of the buffer required, and HX_OK is returned.

IN: Pointer to font IN/OUT: Pointer to buffer for font name, or NULL IN/OUT: Pointer to size of pBuffer

Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if buffer is not large enough for font name.

HxResult HxFontGetReverseStringInWidth ( HxFont_t *  pFont,
const char *  pString,
int32_t *  pWidth,
int32_t *  pBytes 
)

Return the length of a string that fits in width.

HxFontGetReverseStringInWidth returns the number of bytes of a string that can fit into a logical pixel width but the characters are counted in reverse order i.e. from the end of the string. Note that if the string uses multi-byte encoding, the number of bytes and the number of glyphs are not the same.

The string measurement stops when a newline character is found, although the byte count includes the newline character. The byte count does not include the null termination byte.

If pFont is set to NULL, the default system font is used.

Parameters:
pFont IN: Pointer to font, or NULL
pString IN: String to be measured
pWidth IN/OUT: Maximum pixel width for the string On return, the width of the fitted string
pBytes OUT: Return the number of bytes of text that can fit within the logical width.
Returns:
HxResult: If result is not HX_OK, *pBytes is not defined. This function returns HX_OK, with *pBytes set to 0, if the width argument <= 0.

HxResult HxFontGetStringExtents ( HxFont_t *  pFont,
const char *  pString,
HxRectangle_t *  pRectLogical,
HxRectangle_t *  pRectInk 
)

Return the string extents.

HxFontGetStringExtents returns the logical and real extents of the specified UTF-8 string. The logical rectangle describes the typographic extents and should be used to lay out text. The ink rectangle describes the smallest rectangle containing all pixels that are touched when drawing the string. If you only need one of the rectangles, pass NULL for the other one.

The ink rectangle is guaranteed to be a valid rectangle with positive width and height, while the logical rectangle may have negative width indicating right-to-left layout.

The rectangle offsets are reported relative to the baseline and refer to the text being drawn using left alignment. Note that this is a different origin than the default top-left origin used when drawing text.

The string measurement stops when a newline character is found. The count includes the newline character byte.

Note that this function can be used to measure the drawn dimensions of a single glyph (for example, the lower case 'x'), by passing the string "x", setting pRectLogical to NULL, and setting pRectInk to a valid pointer.

If pFont is set to NULL, the default system font is used.

Parameters:
pFont IN: Pointer to font, or NULL
pString IN: String to be measured
pRectLogical OUT: Logical bounds of the string
pRectInk OUT: Real pixel bounds of the string
Returns:
HxResult: If result is not HX_OK, *pRectLogical and *pRectInk are not defined.

HxResult HxFontLoad ( HxFontFamily_t  family,
int32_t  size,
HxFontWeight_t  weight,
HxFontAttributes_t  attributes,
const char *  pFontName,
HxFont_t **  hFont 
)

Load a font.

HxFontLoad returns the HxFont_t structure specified by the arguments. HxFont_t is an opaque structure that is used by the font and string measurement API.

By default, the size is in screen pixels. If the kHxFontAttrPoints attribute is used, size is in points.

pFontName should be set to NULL for system fonts.

If the requested font is not found, the default plain font is returned. An exception to this rule is a request for symbol or wingding fonts: the plain symbol or wingding font is always returned, even when the weight is set to bold and/or italic.

After using the font, unload the font using HxFontUnload.

Parameters:
family IN: See HxFontFamily_t definition
size IN: Size of the font
weight IN: See HxFontWeight_t definition
attributes IN: See HxFontAttributes_t definition
pFontName IN: The name of an application font, or NULL
hFont OUT: Returns HxFont_t if successful
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MISSING_FILE if the requested font and the default font are not found.

HxResult HxFontUnload ( HxFont_t *  pFont  ) 

Unload a font.

HxFontUnload unloads a font that had been loaded through an earlier call to HxFontLoad.

In general, applications should unload fonts that are rarely used in order keep a smaller memory footprint. Internally, a reference count is maintained, so that the font is actually unloaded only after the last user within the application of that particular font calls HxFontUnload.

Parameters:
pFont IN: Pointer to font
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.
